findings.title: Relay residuals: idle live session >10m can dual-emit (ledger no-op); cap-dropped sent copy may be re-relayed while source remains among eight newest files; only eight newest earlier files are candidates.
findings.body: Disclosed limitation (v); ADOPT_QUIET_MS/MAX_SESSIONS_READ=8/enforceCap. Bounded by 7-day age and ledger event_id idempotency. [plugins/dopemux-memory-bridge/hooks/register.tsx] ADJUDICATION: Coordinator: CONFIRMED as the disclosed relay residuals; INFO. Exactly the residuals stated in the amendment record and the prompt: a live session idle for more than 10 minutes can have rows delivered twice (a ledger no-op, `INSERT OR IGNORE` on the event id); a relayed row whose sent copy is later dropped by the 1 MiB cap can be relayed again while the source is among the eight newest earlier files (another no-op, ends at 7 days); a quiet file beyond the eight newest earlier files is not reached until newer files age out, and its rows are lost to the relay after 7 days.

findings.title: safeId can map distinct session ids to one filename (non-alnum collapsed to _), risking ring/file collision for pathological ids.
findings.body: safeId: sessionId.replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9_-]/g, '_').slice(0, 80). Typical UUID-like ids are fine; adversarial or exotic ids could collide under outbox-<key>.jsonl. [plugins/dopemux-memory-bridge/hooks/register.tsx] ADJUDICATION: Coordinator: CONFIRMED in code; LOW; pre-existing and theoretical. `safeId` (`register.tsx:266-269`) replaces characters outside `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` with `_` and truncates to 80, so two session ids that differ only in such characters or after 80 characters would share a file. Claude Code session ids are UUID-shaped (hex and hyphens), which `safeId` maps to themselves, so no real collision is expected. The function dates from the first build commit `e561166a6` and was in both earlier audited heads; it is not a regression of this change. A collision-proof key (for example a short hash suffix) would be a small follow-up.
